title: Air Florida 90
summary: Boeing 737 crashed into the 14th Street Bridge over the Potomac River after takeoff from Washington National Airport on a snowy day. The pilots failed to activate engine anti-ice systems despite heavy snow and below-freezing temperatures, resulting in iced engine inlet sensors. This produced false low engine pressure ratio readings of 1.70 instead of the required 2.04 for takeoff. The aircraft departed with insufficient power and struck the bridge, destroying 97 feet of guard rail before plunging into the icy river. The investigation determined the pilots lacked experience in snowy conditions and failed to follow critical pre-flight procedures.
probable_cause: The pilots failed to activate engine anti-ice systems in freezing conditions with heavy snow, which allowed ice to accumulate on engine inlet probes. False EPR readings indicated insufficient thrust was set, but the pilots nonetheless proceeded with takeoff. The crew's lack of experience flying in snowy weather and failure to follow proper procedures led to insufficient power for flight and crash into the Potomac River.

title: 1982 Thunderbirds Indian Springs Diamond Crash
summary: Four U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds T-38A Talon jets crashed at Indian Springs Air Force Auxiliary Field, Nevada, during formation flying practice of a line abreast loop maneuver. The lead aircraft had a jammed stabilizer that prevented normal pitch control during descent at more than 400 mph. The other three pilots maintained formation in accordance with their training and did not break away, resulting in all four aircraft striking the desert floor almost simultaneously at high speed.
probable_cause: Jammed stabilizer on the lead aircraft prevented recovery during descent. Formation flying procedures and training prevented the wingmen from breaking away when the lead aircraft became uncontrollable.

title: World Airways 30
summary: World Airways Flight 30 touched down 2800 feet beyond the displaced threshold at Boston Logan on a runway covered with ice. Despite poor braking conditions reported as fair to poor, the aircraft could not be stopped on the runway. The pilots steered the aircraft off the runway to avoid obstacles and it skidded across a field and taxiway before coming to rest in Boston Harbor. The cockpit section submerged but 210 occupants survived. Two passengers, father and son, were missing and presumed drowned. A Delta flight had warned of nil braking conditions 35 minutes prior but this was not relayed to Flight 30.

title: Japan Air Lines 350
summary: Japan Air Lines Flight 350, a Douglas DC-8 on final approach to Tokyo, crashed into Tokyo Bay on 9 February 1982, killing 24 of the 174 occupants. The investigation determined the crash resulted from deliberate actions by Captain Katagiri, who disengaged the autopilot and pushed the aircraft into descent at 164 feet altitude despite efforts by the first officer and flight engineer to regain control. Investigators attributed the incident to auditory hallucinations experienced by Katagiri and the absence of proper medical examinations despite his known psychiatric condition.
probable_cause: The accident resulted from deliberate actions of the captain experiencing auditory hallucinations, combined with the failure of medical screening and oversight that allowed him to operate the aircraft despite his mental condition.

First Officer Ishikawa noticed Katagiri's actions and countered by pulling back the yoke on the co-pilot's side to regain control.
Despite their efforts, the DC-8's descent could not be fully arrested.
The aircraft crashed into shallow water 510 meters short of runway 33R.

title: Pilgrim Airlines 458
summary: A de Havilland DHC-6-100 operating from LaGuardia to Boston experienced a fire in the cockpit and cabin caused by leakage of windshield washer fluid containing isopropyl alcohol during cruise. The incompatibility of Tygon tubing with isopropyl alcohol caused the tubing to degrade and separate, allowing flammable fluid to escape and ignite. During descent to Providence, the pilots lost visibility from smoke and were unable to reach the airport, forcing an emergency landing on the frozen Scituate Reservoir near Providence. One passenger could not escape and died of smoke inhalation.

summary: De Havilland DHC-6 Twin Otter Flight 933 crashed into the Barents Sea on 11 March 1982 near Gamvik, Norway, killing all 15 people on board. summary: A Jaguar from 14 Squadron returning from a training mission was accidentally struck by an air-to-air missile fired by a Phantom from 92 Squadron during a station air defence exercise at RAF Wildenrath. title: 1982 British Army Gazelle friendly fire incident
summary: On the night of 5 June 1982 during the Falklands War, British Army Gazelle helicopter XX377 departed Goose Green with a crew of two pilots and two passengers to deliver equipment to a radio rebroadcast station on Pleasant Peak. Believing it to be an Argentine Hercules transport, Cardiff fired two Sea Dart missiles; the second destroyed the aircraft killing all four occupants. The wreckage was initially attributed to enemy fire, but a subsequent inquiry found Cardiff's missiles to be the cause.

title: Aeroflot 411
summary: The Il-62M took off from Sheremetyevo at 12:33 with 80 passengers and 10 crew. Within seconds, engine fire warnings were annunciated for engines one and two. The crew shut down both engines and discharged fire extinguishers. At only 160 meters altitude with the aircraft unable to maintain altitude on two engines with flaps set for takeoff, it stalled at 75 meters above ground and crashed in a forested wetland. Post-crash examination revealed both engines had no pre-crash damage or fire, meaning the fire warnings were false.

summary: On 23 July 1982, a Bell UH-1 Iroquois helicopter was positioned 25 feet above ground hovering near a large mortar effect during filming of Twilight Zone: The Movie at Indian Dunes in Valencia, California. title: Southwest Air Lines 611
summary: The Boeing 737-200 overran the runway while attempting to land at Old Ishigaki Airport on 26 August 1982. The aircraft made a crosswind landing at speed 131 knots, slightly higher than reference airspeed. The aircraft bounced on touchdown and spoilers and thrust reversers did not seem to operate. The flight crew shut down both engines, which disabled the anti-skid braking system. During landing roll, inner tires on both main landing gear burst almost simultaneously. The aircraft overran the runway 145 meters beyond threshold and caught fire at 14:01, destroying the aircraft. All 138 people on board were evacuated and survived, though 67 were injured.

title: 1982 Mannheim helicopter crash
summary: A US Army CH-47C Chinook transport helicopter carrying parachutists on a rehearsal jump took off from Mannheim City Airport. Shortly after takeoff at about 3,000 meters altitude, the pilot reported technical problems and announced a return. During descent at approximately 250 meters, the transmission gearbox failed, causing the two counter-rotating rotor blades to collide and disintegrate. The helicopter lost lift and crashed onto the Bundesautobahn 656, bursting into flames and killing all 46 occupants.

title: Spantax 995
summary: Spantax Flight 995 aborted takeoff from Málaga after the crew detected strong worsening vibration caused by a faulty tire tread failure. Although the abort decision was reasonable, the aircraft was traveling at high speed and lacked sufficient runway to stop, causing it to overrun the runway. During the abort, the captain lost hand control briefly and applied reverse thrust asymmetrically, causing the aircraft to sway left. The aircraft struck airport structures, a highway, vehicles, and buildings before bursting into flames.

However, the aircraft's speed at abort and insufficient remaining runway length caused a runway overrun. Loss of directional control during the abort sequence and asymmetric reverse thrust deployment worsened the excursion.

title: 1982 Bristow Helicopters Bell 212 crash
summary: Bristow Helicopters Bell 212 G-BDIL departed on a medical evacuation mission from the Treasure Finder platform at 2:25 am on September 14, 1982. During darkness, driving rain, and poor visibility, the helicopter searched for the Baffin Seal vessel at very low altitude to locate an injured crewman. The last transmission reported the helicopter five miles north of Murchison platform letting down to surface contact. The helicopter subsequently lost altitude during a right turn while at low altitude and crashed into the North Sea. The investigation found insufficient evidence for a conclusive cause but identified adverse weather, total darkness, and difficult mission profile as major factors.

title: CAAC 2311
summary: CAAC Flight 2311, an Ilyushin Il-18B flying a scheduled domestic route from Changsha to Guangzhou, landed at Baiyun International Airport. After landing, a fire developed in the cabin, apparently started by a passenger's cigarette, producing toxic smoke. The crew stopped the aircraft on the runway and evacuated passengers, but the rapidly developing fire killed 25 passengers and seriously injured 22 passengers and 4 crew members, destroying the aircraft.
